Class ContainerTabs

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ContainerTabs
public final class ContainerTabs extends Object
Tabs on the container screen's panels (7.4.0): a row of tabs, like the creative inventory's, on an edge of the container region's container list or inventory panel. MenuKit draws the row, hit-tests it, and pages it with arrows at its ends when it is wider than its frame; everything a tab is and does is the mod's: what a click does, its icon (anything the mod draws; an item or a sprite ready made), its tooltip, its order, whether it shows and whether it draws selected. MenuKit keeps no selection of its own. 
ContainerTabs.tab("mymod:backpack", ModeScope.BOTH)
        .icon(() -> backpack.stack())
        .tooltip(() -> Component.translatable("mymod.backpack"))
        .on(ContainerScreen.class)
        .order(10)
        .selectedWhen(() -> shown == Shown.BACKPACK)
        .onClick(() -> shown = Shown.BACKPACK)
        .declare();

The row

  • One row per edge per screen. Every mod's tabs on one ContainerTabs.Edge share it, left to right by ContainerTabs.Builder.order, ties by id. A row with no tab showing takes no room.
  • Vanilla's creative tabs, top ones on a top edge and bottom ones on a bottom edge, so they follow a resource pack that restyles those. A selected tab (ContainerTabs.Builder.selectedWhen) runs into the frame, open into it as creative's does; the others stop at it. A disabled one (ContainerTabs.Builder.disabledWhen) is grayed and takes no click.
  • Counted in the layout. The row stands outside its panel, never over a slot, and the region makes room for it: in the block it centers and fits, and in the screen's bounds, so other mods' buttons and recipe viewers keep clear of it. A row between the two panels (the list's bottom edge, the inventory panel's top) stands in the gap between them, widened to hold it.
  • Overflow. Past what fits, vanilla's page arrows at the row's ends move it a tab at a time. A tab that starts drawing selected comes into view. There is no wheel on the row.
  • A click, left button only, runs the tab's ContainerTabs.Builder.onClick with vanilla's click sound, an item on the cursor or not; the click goes no further, so a held item is neither dropped nor placed.

Where a row stands

  • On the region's panels while the region is up (a container screen with a section showing), on any of the four edges.
  • On the screen's own frame (7.4.0) on every other container screen: the player's inventory, a shulker box, a chest with no section showing, a mod's own container screen. A ContainerTabs.Edge.CONTAINERS_TOP row stands on the frame's top edge and an ContainerTabs.Edge.INVENTORY_BOTTOM row on its bottom edge; the two middle edges have no gap to stand in there, and their tabs don't show. The frame and those two rows are centered as one block, as the region's are: the frame moves from vanilla's place (half a top row lower, half a bottom row higher), and everything vanilla places from it with it; a row coming or going lays the screen out again. Screens of one size with the same rows put the row in one place (ScreenFrames makes a shulker box and a chest the inventory's 166), and a mod that opens one in place of another shows a steady row. Only vanilla's own screens move: a mod's own container screen class, a subclass of vanilla's included, may place things from the window itself, so its frame stays where vanilla centers it and its rows stand on it there.
  • A frame that stays (7.5.0, frameStaysWhen(ModeScope, ScreenMatcher, BooleanSupplier)): on the screens a mod chooses, while its condition holds, the frame keeps vanilla's own place and its rows stand in the margin above and below it, so a row coming or going moves nothing. Only where a row wouldn't fit on the window there (a double chest on a short window) does the frame move, and only as far as brings the row inside the 4 px margin; where the frame and its rows don't fit at all, they are centered as above (and a ScreenFrames.scrollsWhenShort(ModeScope, ScreenMatcher) grid scrolls). The condition is read every frame: when it changes the frame's place, the screen is laid out again as for a row change. On the region's panels the inventory panel stays where it stands on a 166 frame at vanilla's place (as on the inventory screen), its sections and rows standing above it, moving only as far as they need to fit; where they don't fit at all, centered as before.
  • Never on the creative inventory, which has tabs of its own.
A row's page carries over to a screen opened in place of the last, and starts over once the player is back in the world.

A tab per key

A mod whose tabs come and go at runtime (one per box the player has open, say) declares a keyed list instead of a tab for each it might ever show. Its keys are read every frame, any type with equals; each key's tab is built the frame the key first appears and kept for as long as it is there, so what MenuKit keeps per tab (the page the row is on, the selected tab kept in view) follows the key wherever the keys move it. The list's tabs stand in the keys' order, together at the list's order among the other tabs, on the frame or the region's panels as any tab does. 
ContainerTabs.keyed("mymod:boxes", ModeScope.BOTH, () -> boxes.open())
        .tab((box, t) -> t
                .icon(box::stack)
                .tooltip(() -> box.stack().getHoverName())
                .selectedWhen(() -> box.equals(shown))
                .onClick(() -> shown = box))
        .on(InventoryScreen.class, ContainerScreen.class, ShulkerBoxScreen.class)
        .order(200)
        .declare();

Groups

A keyed list with a header is a group: a header tab, and the keys' tabs after it as its sub-tabs, smaller by default and standing on the same line. Groups are the mod's to use or not, and everything about one is the mod's but how it moves:
  • What a header click does is its own onClick: show the header's own page, or pick its first sub-tab.
  • When its sub-tabs are out is ContainerTabs.Keyed.expandedWhen(BooleanSupplier), read every frame: always, only while the group holds the selected tab, or on the mod's own conditions.
  • How they move is MenuKit's, one way only: they slide out from under the header to its right as the group opens, the tabs after it moving over to make room, and slide back under it as it closes, eased alike each way. A turn mid-way goes back from where they are. A slide that makes the row page opens the arrows' room with it, so the tabs move over rather than jump; a tab shows whole or not at all. A group stands as it is on a screen's first frame, so opening the inventory doesn't play it.
  • Paging counts the tabs out: a closed group is its header, an open one its header and every sub-tab, and the arrows page through those. A closed group's sub-tabs take no click.
  • Pinned tabs (ContainerTabs.Builder.pinnedWhen), a header or a sub-tab, stay in view while the row is paged either way past them: each stops at the end of the row it would leave by, the tabs beyond it going on behind it, and pinned tabs of one group stand there side by side in row order, until the next group's header (at the left end) or the previous group's pinned tabs (at the right end) push them off together, as section headers do in a phone's list. Which tabs pin is the mod's, read every frame: a header while its group is open, a sub-tab while it is selected.
ContainerTabs.keyed("mymod:chest", ModeScope.BOTH, () -> chestBoxes())
        .header(h -> h
                .icon(() -> new ItemStack(Items.CHEST))
                .selectedWhen(() -> shown == CHEST)
                .onClick(() -> shown = CHEST))
        .tab((box, t) -> t
                .icon((g, x, y, w, h) -> drawBox(g, box, x, y, w, h))   // the mod's own drawing
                .selectedWhen(() -> box.equals(shown))
                .onClick(() -> shown = box))
        .expandedWhen(() -> keepAllOpen || groupOf(shown) == CHEST)
        .order(200)
        .declare();

Groups that come and go

A mod whose groups come and go at runtime (one per open box that holds boxes, say) declares a list of groups: its group keys are read every frame as a keyed list's keys are, and each is a group as ContainerTabs.Keyed.header makes one, with a header and its own keys' sub-tabs, built the frame the key first appears and kept for as long as it is there. The groups stand in the group keys' order, one after another, together at the list's order.

Nested groups (7.5.0). A group whose key is also one of another live group's keys stands inside that group, in place of the sub-tab that key would have: its header where the sub-tab was, its own sub-tabs after it, then the rest of the parent's. So a box opened inside a chest stays where its tab was, [Chest] a b [Box ▸ its boxes] c d, at any depth. The nested group slides out from under its own header as any group does, and goes under its parent's header with the parent's sub-tabs when the parent closes; its tabs are in the row only while every group above it is expanded. A tab pinned in a nested group pins the headers of every group its own group stands in, so paged past, the chain stands at the row's end side by side (ContainerTabs.Builder.pinnedWhen). A key that is its own group's key stays a sub-tab, and a group stands in one place only: the first group to hold it, in row order. Groups that stand among each other belong in one list. 

ContainerTabs.groups("mymod:boxes", ModeScope.BOTH, () -> tree.groups(), group -> group.boxesInside())
        .header((group, h) -> h
                .icon(group::stack)
                .selectedWhen(() -> group.equals(shown))
                .onClick(() -> shown = group))
        .tab((group, box, t) -> t
                .icon(box::stack)
                .selectedWhen(() -> box.equals(shown))
                .onClick(() -> shown = box))
        .expandedWhen(group -> group.holds(shown))
        .order(200)
        .declare();

Size and icons

ContainerTabs.Builder.size(int, int) sets a tab's width and height, and ContainerTabs.Keyed.tabSize(int, int) every key's tab's. A tab's icon is the mod's own drawing (ContainerTabs.Builder.icon(Icon)), every frame, in an icon box 16 px square on a full-size tab and smaller in proportion on a smaller one: an item, a sprite, an animation, anything. The item and sprite forms are that, ready made.

To show one container at a time under the tabs, as the creative inventory shows one page, give each section a visibleWhen that reads the mod's own pick, have each tab's onClick set it, and declare the screen fitted, so the frame fits the one shown.

Declare from your client initializer: tabs freeze with every other declaration.

    • TAB_WIDTH

      public static final int TAB_WIDTH
      A tab's default width: vanilla's 26 px tab. Tabs stand side by side, touching, so no background shows between them.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TAB_HEIGHT

      public static final int TAB_HEIGHT
      A tab's default height beyond the frame edge it stands on: vanilla's creative top tab stands 28 px above its frame, these 25, room for a full-size icon inside an unpicked tab with two rows clear above and below it. A double chest with a row above it needs 245 px (212 + 25 and the two margins), so in a 240 px window its grid scrolls by 5.

      Starts a keyed list of tabs, its id namespaced and unique among tabs and lists ("mymod:boxes"), for one mode scope: one tab per key keys gives, read every frame a container screen is open, in the order it gives them.       Starts a list of groups, its id namespaced and unique among tabs and lists ("mymod:boxes"), for one mode scope: one group per key groups gives, read every frame a container screen is open, in the order it gives them, and in each group one sub-tab per key keys gives for it, read every frame as a keyed list's are.
